subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should direct `read` calls on PDF and Office documents use a narrow unsupported-document fallback, native document parsing, or defer to the broader file-input architecture?
rationale: The source-level token-waste problem is real, but the permanent boundary changes whether `read` remains text/image-only or grows document parsing and security-sensitive file handling.

options.title: Narrow read fallback
options.body: Return a bounded, actionable unsupported-document message for PDF/Office formats and keep document extraction in existing PDF or future document tools.

options.title: Core document parsing
options.body: Approve parser dependencies and resource limits before adding native DOCX/PPTX/XLSX extraction to the read path.

options.title: Defer to file-input work
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the broader provider-native and binary upload trackers until that architecture is chosen.

recommendation.title: Narrow read fallback
recommendation.body: Return a bounded, actionable unsupported-document message for PDF/Office formats and keep document extraction in existing PDF or future document tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core read-tool behavior, media/file intake, and safety defaults, and this owner has the strongest history across those surfaces in the inspected commits.
